**`confirmed_fatal` — `dependency_citation`. Repaired. All gates clean. The level is not ready for step 9, and my step-8 report undercounted the reason.**

## The adjudication

DeepSeek is right. I opened `thm-fubini-over-a-region-between-continuous-graphs` on disk: every quantifier in it is over the vertical orientation, and it has no symmetric clause — unlike its sibling `thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections`, which explicitly carries one. `def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions` is likewise careful to claim Jordan measurability only for "each **Type I description**." The library states this Fubini for one orientation and knows it.

[L3] dropped the word "vertical" and applied the result to a Type II region. That is not a loose paraphrase of a fact that covers the use — **a Type II region is not an instance of the cited theorem at all** — and it was load-bearing: step 3.1 needed `D` Jordan measurable and `∂ₓQ` integrable over it, and nothing else in the item supplied either.

Not nonfatal, on my own step-8 line: the named route fails *and* no correct one is immediate from the item's declared facts. Closing it requires importing a theorem the item does not reach. The tell is the asymmetry — neither lane touched the Type I twin, whose [L3] restates the same theorem exactly and applies it to literally the theorem's `K`. Terra's pass reason named every part of the proof except the part that was wrong, so I did not weigh it against the cross-family lane.

The Statement was never false, though — this is an unclosable-gap fatal, not a false-assertion fatal, and I said so in the report rather than flattening the distinction.

## The repair

Statement unchanged. I did not take the cheap fix of narrowing to elementary regions. [L3] narrowed to what Jordan–Fubini gives; four exact facts added ([L5]–[L8]); **new step 1.3 writes the transpose**: `σ(x,y)=(y,x)` is linear and involutive, `σ(D)` is a graph-region over its *first* coordinate so [L6] applies, and [L7] returns `D = σ(σ(D))` as a bounded Jordan set. New step 2.2 discharges the remaining Fubini hypotheses. Three published deps added; `depcheck`/`fwdcheck` clean. Batch-4 proof contract updated in step (its step-1.2 claim had been stale since step 8).

**Converging, not thrashing.** Three touches, three distinct defects in three different parts of the argument — endpoint sections, then that repair's own false endpoint identity, then the measure-theoretic prerequisites. The Type II case does not need a different route; it needed the route the library already owns and the item was not citing.

## Impact

`research/frontier-12-impact-audit.json` written and validated (exit 0) against `--from pre-step8 --to after-alpha-step8b` — **use that pair, not `after-alpha-step8`**; it covers both changed interfaces. All five consumers read in full, all disposed. On your specific question: **no consumer leaned on the false direction**, and structurally couldn't have — in both potential consumers the path-connected set is the corollary's own domain `U`, never a proper subset, and the false direction only bites for a proper subset.

- **`plan_reconciliation` is 127 items, not 14.** My step-8 report read a truncated tail of the gate output and called it the whole set — all fourteen names I listed ran `thm-s`…`thm-z`, which should have told me. I filled my own row; **126 remain**, and they're authorship records, not adjudications.
- **`audit-receipt-manifest` appeared because of this repair.** My three added edges changed the relationship set. I refreshed `manifest_sha256` and wrote the limitation into the attestation text so it can't read as re-attesting the 126 open rows.

Better news: `spine-receipt-invalid` is **closed** — the spine receipt now exists and is valid, including after my edit.
